ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993 (sections 19-24, 89-95 and 188-190); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Amendment Act 2023; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Income Tax Act 2007; and the Companies Office practice of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment. Beneficial ownership information is obtained by reporting entities under the AML/CFT Act and is accessible to government supervisors, but New Zealand maintains no public UBO register; accordingly, UBO disclosure is Government_Only_Access.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, each proposed director, shareholder, beneficial owner, officer, authorised signatory and source-of-funds counterparty must be screened against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit PEP indicators; the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade sanctions list maintained under the United Nations Act 1946 and the Russia Sanctions Act 2022; the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; and, where a US, UK or EU nexus exists, the UK Consolidated List and EU financial sanctions lists. Screening must use exact and fuzzy matching on names, addresses, date of birth and passport/ID numbers, with manual review of all positive hits and near-hit alerts. Any positive PEP or sanctions match requires enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and source of funds verification, senior compliance officer approval and, in an unresolved case, refusal of the incorporation engagement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12 (Incorporation), 37 (Share Capital), 122 (Registered Office), 128 (Appointment of Directors), 131 (Duties of Directors), and 153 (Financial Reporting); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (if offering securities to the public); Real Estate Agents Act 2008 (if engaging in real estate agency activities, but not applicable for passive REIT holding).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating through the Companies Register online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN/01 – Application for Registration of a Company (Incorporation), filed electronically via the Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement for a limited liability company. However, the company must have at least one share issued and one shareholder. The board may resolve to issue shares for consideration in cash or non-cash assets, and any unpaid capital must be recorded in the company's financial statements. No escrow or blocked account is mandated by statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company') — ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING PURSUANT TO SECTION 122(2) OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 AND THE COMPANY'S CONSTITUTION. 

RESOLVED THAT: 

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The board hereby approves the allotment and issuance of [NUMBER] ordinary shares of no par value to the initial subscriber(s) as set forth in the incorporation application, at a subscription price of [AMOUNT] per share, payable in full in cash or in kind as approved by the board. The board confirms that the aggregate consideration received or receivable for such shares is adequate and that the shares are validly issued, fully paid or credited as fully paid, and rank pari passu in all respects. The board authorizes the Company Secretary to file the necessary return of allotment with the New Zealand Companies Office within the statutory period. 

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The board hereby approves the opening of corporate bank accounts with [BANK NAME] (the 'Bank') and authorizes the following individuals, acting singly or jointly as specified, to operate such accounts: [DIRECTOR 1 NAME], [DIRECTOR 2 NAME], and [COMPANY SECRETARY NAME]. The board authorizes the execution of all account opening documents, mandates, and any related agreements, and further authorizes the Bank to honor all cheques, drafts, electronic transfers, and other instruments drawn on or payable from the Company's accounts when signed by any two authorized signatories. The board ratifies any prior actions taken in this regard. 

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The board hereby adopts the registered office of the Company at [FULL ADDRESS], New Zealand, as the official address for service of documents and legal notices, and confirms that the address is a physical location (not a post office box) and that the Company's records are maintained at this address. The board authorizes the Company Secretary to file the notice of registered office with the Companies Office and to update the register as required. 

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The board hereby appoints [DIRECTOR 1 NAME] and [DIRECTOR 2 NAME] as directors of the Company, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until earlier resignation or removal. The board further appoints [COMPANY SECRETARY NAME] as the Company Secretary, who shall be responsible for maintaining statutory registers, filing annual returns, and ensuring compliance with the Companies Act 1993. The board acknowledges the directors' duties under sections 131-138 of the Act, including the duty to act in good faith and in the best interests of the Company. 

5. GENERAL: The board authorizes any director or the Company Secretary to execute all documents, make all filings, and take all steps necessary to give effect to this resolution. This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts. 

DATED this [DAY] day of [MONTH], [YEAR]. 

SIGNED by the Directors: 
___________________________ 
[DIRECTOR 1 NAME] 
___________________________ 
[DIRECTOR 2 NAME]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Company Constitution Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) – Online Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application via the Companies Register online portal. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and must not contain restricted words unless consent is obtained. For a REIT, the name may include 'Trust' or 'REIT' but must not imply a registered bank unless authorized. Simultaneously, prepare and adopt a company constitution (or rely on the default constitution under the Companies Act 1993). The constitution must be signed by all initial shareholders and directors. The name reservation is valid for 20 working days. If the name is rejected, the applicant will receive a notice with reasons and may submit an alternative name or appeal to the Registrar within 10 working days.
required_dossiers: Consent from any person whose name is used
Copy of the proposed constitution (if not adopting default)
Identification documents of the applicant (passport or driver's license)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a formal objection with the Companies Office within 10 working days, providing evidence of distinctiveness or consent. Alternatively, select a new name and re-submit. For constitution issues, the Registrar may provide a notice of non-compliance; amend and re-file within 15 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) – Online Incorporation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form NZCN/01 (Application for Registration of a Company) electronically. The application must include the company name, registered office address (must be a physical address in New Zealand), postal address (if different), the full names, addresses, and dates of birth of all directors and shareholders, and the number of shares to be issued. The application must be accompanied by the consent of each director to act in that capacity. The incorporation fee is payable online. Upon successful filing, the Registrar will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and a unique NZBN (New Zealand Business Number). The company is deemed incorporated on the date of the certificate. Ensure all information is accurate; any false statements may lead to penalties.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (signed by each director)
Consent to act as shareholder (if not the same as director)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the Registrar will issue a notice of deficiency. The applicant must respond within 20 working days with the required corrections. If the application is suspended, the applicant may request a review by the Registrar or appeal to the High Court. Common issues include incomplete director details or invalid registered office; rectify and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) – Online Compliance Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 10 working days of incorporation, the company must file a notice of registered office (Form NZCN/02) and a notice of appointment of directors (Form NZCN/03) if not already included in the incorporation application. The company must also establish and maintain a share register, a director's register, and a register of charges (if any). The company secretary (if appointed) must be recorded. For a REIT, if the company intends to offer units to the public, it must also register a prospectus under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) – this is a separate process. The company must also obtain an IRD number from Inland Revenue for tax purposes and register for GST if annual turnover exceeds NZD 60,000. The Companies Office will automatically issue an NZBN, but the IRD number must be applied for separately.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the company fails to file the required notices, the Registrar may issue a compliance notice with a deadline of 20 working days. Non-compliance may result in a fine of up to NZD 10,000. For IRD issues, contact Inland Revenue to rectify any delays; penalties may apply for late registration. If the FMA queries the prospectus, the company must respond within the specified timeframe or withdraw the offer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Financial Services Licensing Assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Banks (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac) and Financial Markets Authority (FMA) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account with a licensed New Zealand bank. The bank will require the Certificate of Incorporation, the company constitution, a resolution of the board authorizing the account, and identification of all signatories. For a REIT, the bank may conduct enhanced due diligence on the source of funds and the trust structure. If the REIT is publicly offered, the company must obtain a license from the FMA under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (managed investment scheme license). For a private REIT, no FMA license is required, but the company must comply with the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and prepare financial statements in accordance with NZ IFRS. The company must also appoint an auditor if it meets the threshold (total assets > NZD 30 million or revenue > NZD 15 million).
required_dossiers: Identification of directors and shareholders (passport, proof of address)
Business plan or trust deed (for REIT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application, the company may provide additional documentation or apply to another bank. If the FMA requires a license and the application is incomplete, the FMA will issue a notice of deficiency; the company has 30 days to respond. If the license is refused, the company may appeal to the FMA's independent tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for financial services licensing; for physical property management, the local territorial authority (e.g., Auckland Council) issues building and resource consents; for any physical construction or operation of real estate, the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) oversees building regulations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Managed Investment Scheme (MIS) License (if public REIT) or Financial Advice Provider License (if providing financial advice); for property operations, a Resource Consent and Building Consent from the local council.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For a real estate investment trust that only holds passive income-generating properties (e.g., commercial or residential rentals), the EIA requirement is typically 'Exempt' or 'Environmental Registration' if the properties are existing and no new construction is involved. If the trust undertakes new development or significant redevelopment, a 'Full EIA Report' may be required under the Resource Management Act 1991. The classification is determined by the scale and location of the project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For existing buildings, compliance with the Building Act 2004 and the Resource Management Act 1991 is required. Wastewater discharges must meet the National Environmental Standards for Sources of Human Drinking Water (NES-DW) and the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ). For hazardous waste, the Hazardous Substances (Hazardous Waste) Regulations 2004 apply. Specific quantitative thresholds: for wastewater, the maximum allowable concentration of biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is 20 mg/L, total suspended solids (TSS) 30 mg/L, and pH 6-9. For volatile organic compounds (VOCs), the ambient air standard is 0.5 mg/m³ over 24 hours. For hazardous waste, the facility must obtain a waste management permit and comply with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) Act 2017. Each building must have a current Fire Evacuation Scheme approved by FENZ. Structural load inspections are mandated by the Building Act 2004, requiring a Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) for buildings with specified systems (e.g., fire alarms, sprinklers). Occupational safety clearance is issued by WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, requiring a documented health and safety plan and regular audits. For a REIT, the property manager must ensure all tenants comply with these requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tāke), Wellington; online portal myIR at www.ird.govt.nz, supplemented by New Zealand Companies Office for corporate registration and New Zealand Customs Service for export declarations
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand incorporated limited company, the New Zealand Companies Office issues the NZBN at incorporation and Inland Revenue automatically allocates the IRD number used for income tax and GST. If automatic allocation has not occurred, or a foreign non-resident company needs to register for New Zealand tax, the entity must: (1) obtain a NZBN or provide an overseas company registration certificate equivalent; (2) lodge a non-resident company IRD number application through myIR, supplying legal name, country of incorporation, registered office and residential agent details, director information, principal place or place of business, expected first taxable period, and the scope of New Zealand activities; (3) use the same IRD number as the GST number, as New Zealand does not issue a separate VAT identification number; (4) register for GST under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 through myIR when taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, or voluntarily where allowed, selecting the filing frequency and accounting basis; (5) appoint a New Zealand agent or contact address for tax notices if the company has no physical New Zealand office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a New Zealand limited company is a separate taxpaying person resident in New Zealand if incorporated in New Zealand; it is taxed on worldwide income at the standard corporate rate of 28%; there is no automatic pass-through classification for a limited company and no tax-exempt zone treatment; a qualifying close company may elect Look-Through Company status under the Income Tax Act 2007, and a qualifying portfolio investment vehicle may elect Portfolio Investment Entity rules)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include: Look-Through Company election for close companies; Portfolio Investment Entity election for qualifying investment entities; voluntary GST registration; GST accounting basis elections (payments basis, invoice basis, or hybrid basis); GST return frequency election; and non-resident supplier remote-services GST registration. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 are self-executing and do not require an elective filing mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) Act 1985 - New Zealand value-added tax regime
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000; compulsory when taxable supplies made in New Zealand exceed this threshold in any rolling 12-month period, subject to limited exceptions for non-resident suppliers of remote services who may need simplified registration irrespective of the threshold; voluntary registration is available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance mandate, mandatory continuous transaction control, or anti-fraud digital stamping system. E-invoicing through the Peppol network is voluntary. GST-registered persons must issue tax invoices containing the prescribed particulars under the GST Act 1985, retain complete records for at least seven years, and file GST returns electronically through myIR on a monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly basis depending on turnover and election.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST-registered person may claim 0% GST on exported goods where the goods are physically removed from New Zealand and contemporaneous export evidence is retained. Services may be zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient outside New Zealand and not directly connected with New Zealand land. A real estate investment trust earning rental income from New Zealand real property cannot treat domestic property income as export zero-rated; the zero-rating regime applies only to genuine offshore supplies of goods or qualifying services, not to New Zealand land-based income.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs export declaration (Export Entry) lodged electronically through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window system with customs reference number
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing goods are physically consigned from New Zealand to the overseas buyer
Commercial invoice, packing list, and supply contract supporting the zero-rated transaction

Bank foreign exchange inward remittance/SWIFT credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds (FIRC is an Indian banking instrument and is not a New Zealand statutory document, but bank-generated foreign exchange credit evidence is accepted)
Freight, port, vessel/voyage records and insurance certificate proving departure from New Zealand territory
GST tax invoice for the zero-rated supply and any related agency or logistics agreements
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit export zero-rating claims and withdraw zero-rating where the goods are not exported, the services do not meet statutory recipient tests, tax invoices are absent, or export proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day foreign exchange deadline. The supply is recharacterized as taxable at 15% GST with use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties imposed under the Tax Administration Act 1994, ranging from 20% for lack of reasonable care up to 150% for evasion or abusive tax positions. Directors and controlling shareholders can incur personal liability for outstanding GST clawbacks in cases of deliberate or reckless non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a lawfully unrestricted foreign exchange regime. The New Zealand dollar is freely floating under the Reserve Bank Act 1989, without curbs on current account transactions, trade settlement, capital transfers, dividends, or profit remittance. Non-resident shareholders may hold local bank accounts and repatriate distributions once the board declares a dividend and withholding tax formalities are observed. There is no surrender ratio and no central bank licence required for payment execution. The only possible conditional barrier is the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which requires consent for non-residents acquiring sensitive land; a real estate investment trust must obtain Overseas Investment Office clearance or a statutory exemption and demonstrate that the trust portfolio is not strategically sensitive. New Zealand's Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 imposes bank-level verification, but that is a documentary control, not an exchange restriction. In practice, Tier-1 banks can complete conversion to NZD at market rate and execute cross-border wires in major currencies without administrative bottlenecks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion rules apply; the mandatory conversion ratio is 0. Exporters may retain 100% of export receipts in NZD or foreign currency at any licensed bank, use them directly for onward trade payments, or convert at market rate at a time of their choosing. There is no forced timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational NZD/USD Treasury Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational NZD/Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational NZD Account with Forex Dealing Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low, 2 out of 10, and legally constrained for the primary banking rail. In New Zealand, an offshore digital EMI is not a registered bank and generally cannot accept public deposits or provide unrestricted payment services under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. Most offshore EMIs operate under a foreign e-money licence and are not participants in Payments NZ clearing, meaning they cannot receive or issue funds through New Zealand bank account numbers, cannot provide settlement finality, and cannot support the required capital verification trail for a REIT. They also create avoidable ML/TF friction and audit risk when used as the sole liquidity vehicle. Offshore EMIs should be restricted to marginal auxiliary collections only and must never be used as the capital escrow, dividend distribution engine, or treasury clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandated: for the statutory director of a New Zealand incorporated REIT, in-branch physical identity verification is required in nearly all Tier-1 banks. Remote consular proxy opening is not automatic; a bank may accept a verified overseas interview only if the entity is low risk, all documents are certified and legalised, and the overseas branch is pre-approved, but this remains discretionary and typically requires a New Zealand resident director to co-sign. The company should appoint a New Zealand resident director and produce board resolutions, trust deeds, ownership charts, company extracts, and passport-level identity documentation in English to accelerate onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership obscured by a multi-layered trust or offshore corporate holding structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified company registration document for every entity in the chain; authenticated trust deed listing settlor, trustees, protector and discretionary beneficiaries; graphical ownership structure; passport copies and proof of address for all natural persons with 25% or more economic interest; independent tax and accounting office confirmation of the ultimate senior beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds opacity on capital contribution intended to purchase real estate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed wealth acquisition narrative; personal or corporate bank statements for 6 to 12 months; purchase or sale agreements, inheritance certificate, gift deed, dividend voucher, or private equity exit statement; independent accountant letter tracing the capital in NZD or foreign currency to the shareholder; no unexplained cash deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax residency and foreign reporting mismatch of non-resident directors and beneficiaries under CRS and New Zealand FATCA regime.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original tax residency certificates from each relevant jurisdiction; signed CRS self-certification; FATCA classification for any US affiliate; IRD tax file number if applicable; registered office letter; independent legal opinion confirming that the trust is not an opaque passive investment vehicle and that distribution withholding taxes are correctly documented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to regulated sensitive land and sanctions risk embedded in the real estate portfolio.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificates of title for each property; Overseas Investment Office clearance or statutory exemption letter; zoning certificate; board resolution confirming the trust limits its activity to low-risk income-generating commercial property; sanction list screening against UN, OFAC, and EU lists for all counterparties; audited financial statements of the trust.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must arrive by SWIFT wire (MT103) from the shareholder own bank account, with the ordering customer name matching the beneficial shareholder and the narrative stating capital contribution to NZ Ltd REIT and the BOP/international transactions purpose code for equity capital. The receiving bank holds funds in a capital escrow account until board allotment; the company files the share return with the New Zealand Companies Office. Capital verification is completed by reconciling the deposit ticket, the company share register, and the board resolution. If the REIT acquires sensitive land, a supporting Overseas Investment Office clearance must be attached before the injection is authorised.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade disbursements ride on SWIFT MT103 for clean payments; commercial letters of credit are opened through MT700 with the advising bank, and documentary collections D/P and D/A are processed via the same correspondent network. New Zealand domestic vendor payments use Payments NZ local clearing rails including bulk electronic clearing, while high-value domestic settlement runs through the Reserve Bank settlement account system. Cross-border beneficiary payments route via SWIFT, and dividend or trust distributions are reported in the bank balance of payments return and executed with an MT103 carrying the beneficiary tax details.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable NZD forward FX contracts executed under an ISDA CSA with a Tier-1 New Zealand bank for matching known NZD income or distribution dates.
FX swaps for near-dated conversion of NZD into a second currency and re-swapping back on a later value date.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps to hedge foreign-currency non-recourse REIT debt or long-term offshore investor currency exposure.
Non-deliverable forwards are permissible but economically redundant for NZD because the currency is fully convertible; they are accepted only when a foreign counterparty cannot physically settle NZD.
Vanilla FX option purchases are accessible for approved treasury hedging under an ALCO derivative limit and are not permitted for speculative gains.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Register annual confirmation filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 calendar days after the annual return date, which is normally the anniversary of incorporation unless the company has elected a different annual return date with the Registrar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing penalty of NZD 50 (approx. USD 30) is imposed by the Companies Office. If the annual return remains unfiled, the Registrar issues a formal default notice, and if the default continues, the company is liable to administrative strike-off from the Companies Register. Directors commit an offence under the Companies Act 1993 and may each be fined up to NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000); upon removal the company is dissolved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements with independent auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the balance date for a large company, an issuer, or an overseas company filing under the Companies Act 1993; for a listed REIT, the annual report and financial statements must also be delivered to NZX within 4 months after balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver financial statements is a Companies Act offence; each director is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000). The Registrar may also take enforcement action and, for a listed/FMC reporting entity, the Financial Markets Authority and NZX can impose pecuniary penalties, public censure, or suspension for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual significant controller / UBO confirmation in the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand Companies Register (integrated in the annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same 28-day annual return window as the Annual Return; any new significant controller, cessation, or change in significant control must be notified within 30 calendar days of the event and before the annual return filing is made.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Keeping a false or incomplete significant controller register is an offence under the Companies Act 1993, exposing the company and each defaulting director to fines of up to NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000). Persistent UBO failures can be treated as a corporate governance default justifying a Registrar compliance notice and ultimately strike-off in combination with other filing defaults.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: FMC reporting entity annual disclosure / managed investment scheme fund update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA), New Zealand, together with Companies Office and NZX if listed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 4 months after balance date for a listed FMC reporting entity; if the REIT is a licensed managed investment scheme not NZX-listed, the scheme's annual update and financial statements follow the scheme registration disclosure cycle under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance may result in civil pecuniary penalties under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, FMA injunction orders, and revocation or suspension of the REIT/manager licence; NZX listed securities may be suspended or delisted for continuing disclosure failures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is triggered for any FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, which includes a licensed real estate investment trust, managed investment scheme, or listed issuer; no size threshold applies to that category. In addition, a New Zealand company is 'large' and must be audited if, in each of the two immediately preceding accounting periods, the consolidated total assets exceed NZD 60 million (approx. USD 36 million) or consolidated total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million (approx. USD 18 million). New Zealand does not impose a separate headcount threshold as an audit trigger for for-profit companies. The audit must be performed by a licensed auditor holding a Certificate of Public Practice issued by Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ) or an equivalent NZX/FMA-recognised assurance practitioner.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP) established by the External Reporting Board (XRB). For-profit entities must apply New Zealand equivalents of International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS); eligible small and medium-sized entities may apply NZ IFRS for SMEs. An FMC reporting REIT must apply NZ IFRS and comply with the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and NZX Listing Rules (where applicable).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Act 1993, every company must maintain an internal significant controller (UBO) register and must confirm and update that information in its annual return each year. A notifiable event, such as a shareholding transfer that creates, changes, or ceases a significant controller, must be recorded in the significant controller register and reported through the Companies Office within 30 calendar days of the event. Share transfers in general must be registered in the Register of Members within 10 working days after being lodged with the company. The annual return must be signed off by a director and filed within 28 days after the annual return date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (board and shareholder meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 - USD 500 per annum (NZD 200 - NZD 800) for a professional registered office and company secretarial agent in New Zealand
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 40,000 per annum for an independently audited REIT vehicle, increasing to USD 40,000 - USD 100,000 for larger multi-property trusts

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand has no free-zone or REIT-specific tax holiday; a New Zealand LTD pays the flat 28% company tax rate. The imputation credit system prevents economic double taxation of resident shareholders; a 15% R&D tax credit is available for eligible research and development; portfolio investment entity rules may apply if the REIT is a listed PIE, but no preferential corporate income tax rate is granted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - Company Income Tax Return (and IR4N for non-resident companies carrying on business in New Zealand only through a fixed establishment or having only New Zealand-sourced income); filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR Business Gateway.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March standard balance date, the IR4 must be filed on or before 7 July. For a non-standard balance date, the due date is the 7th day of the fourth month after the balance date, unless a tax agent extension has been granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable income including gross rental income, property sales, management fees, interest, and other business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company must include only New Zealand-sourced income in Box 1. Foreign investment income of a non-resident is not assessable except where income is attributable to a New Zealand fixed establishment or the company is a transitional resident; dividend and interest income from New Zealand is separately reportable through the NRWT payment process rather than IR4 Box 1 for non-resident withholding income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: property rates, insurance, repairs, depreciation, interest, management fees, professional fees, and legal costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest deductions by a non-resident-controlled NZ company may be restricted by the thin capitalisation rules under Income Tax Act 2007 subpart FE; non-resident companies must not deduct notional head-office overhead unless the expense is incurred in deriving New Zealand taxable income and satisfies the arm's length transfer pricing standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deduction of available losses and before tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies carrying on business in New Zealand through a fixed establishment must ensure losses claimed are sourced from New Zealand activities and are supported by the tax loss continuity rules; the IR4N schedule requires separate statement of New Zealand-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company tax computed at 28% of net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident companies, the 28% rate applies to New Zealand-source business income; dividends and interest derived by non-residents are not included here if subject to NRWT and are reported on separate NRWT returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Imputation credits, RWT, PAYE, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits attached to income or deducted at source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate shareholder cannot generally use New Zealand imputation credits against NRWT; imputation credits are attached to the dividend and reduce certain resident shareholder tax but do not eliminate the 30% NRWT unless a DTA provides a lower rate. The NZ company must file an imputation return separately for credits attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Residual income tax / refund and NRWT declaration schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final liability after credits; overpayments are refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company is not carrying on business through a New Zealand fixed establishment, it may not file IR4 at all; instead, the payer is required to withhold NRWT and the non-resident beneficiary may claim a refund of excess WHT under a DTA. The IR4 must disclose outbound dividends paid to non-residents, triggering NRWT obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of IR4 attracts automatic late-filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994, with initial penalties and incremental daily penalties; residual tax remains subject to use of money interest. Deliberate failure to file, false declarations, or evasion is an offence under sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994: a body corporate may be fined up to NZD 100,000 and directors may be fined up to NZD 50,000 and/or imprisoned for up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on the gross dividend paid to non-residents
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the NZ payer must obtain from the non-resident beneficial owner before payment: (1) a completed Inland Revenue IR290 non-resident withholding tax and declaration of tax residency form; (2) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the recipient's jurisdiction; (3) written confirmation of beneficial ownership and entitlement to treaty benefits, including satisfactory evidence that the recipient is not used for treaty shopping; and (4) the payer reduces the withholding rate at source only where the DTA article permits. If excess NRWT is withheld, the non-resident must file a refund claim with Inland Revenue attaching the TRC and supporting dividends, interest, or royalty vouchers.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 15% NRWT; an Approved Issuer Levy of 2% may apply to interest paid on publicly issued bonds by approved issuers in lieu of NRWT. Under most NZ DTAs, interest is reduced to 10% or 0%, and royalties are typically reduced to 5% or 10% depending on the treaty and IP characterisation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10 million aggregate cross-border related-party transactions (IRD contemporaneous documentation benchmark); Country-by-Country reporting applies if the worldwide group has consolidated revenue of EUR 750m or more, requiring a New Zealand master/local file equivalent.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand applies economic substance principles through the general anti-avoidance rule under Income Tax Act 2007 section BG 1 and through CFC attribution and place of effective management tests. For a REIT SPV, Core Income-Generating Activities must actually be performed in New Zealand: asset management, leasing negotiations, property maintenance, financing decisions, and board governance. A tax-haven shell with no real staff, premises, or decision-making power will not satisfy New Zealand tax residence or treaty entitlement and may be recharacterised with penal adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting gross rental income from the real estate portfolio, fabricating deductible expenses, or filing a materially false IR4 to reduce corporate income tax and outbound NRWT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 1994 sections 143A and 143B: criminal fine of up to NZD 100,000 for a body corporate and up to NZD 50,000 for an individual; civil shortfall penalties up to 150% of the avoided tax under the shortfall penalty regime of the Tax Administration Act 1994; use of money interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign or procure a false return may be convicted personally, imprisoned for up to 5 years, and barred from managing companies; the court may pierce the corporate veil, order restitution of diverted funds, and Inland Revenue may issue a departure prohibition order preventing overseas travel until tax debts are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the NZ_LTD as a brass-plate shell with no employees, no New Zealand premises, no substantive board meetings, and no real estate management function, using the NZ entity solely to access tax treaty benefits or shelter profits from the REIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 section BG 1 general anti-avoidance and section GB 1 reconstruction of income; shortfall penalties for abusive tax position up to 100% of the tax avoided; Companies Act 1993 sections 135 and 136 for reckless trading and failure to perform director duties; Financial Reporting Act 2013 penalties for false financial statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Companies Act 1993 section 301, directors can be personally ordered to repay money or restore property to the company or creditors; directors may be disqualified for up to 5 years or more; if the shell is used to evade tax, directors face criminal imprisonment under the Tax Administration Act, and blacklisting or travel restrictions may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting high-value cash from property investors, distributing trust income without customer due diligence, failing to report suspicious transactions, or operating without an AML/CFT programme where the REIT falls within the definition of a reporting entity or high-value dealer under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: civil penalties of up to NZD 2 million for a body corporate and up to NZD 200,000 per individual; separate criminal liability for money laundering under the Crimes Act 1961 sections 243 to 243A; suspension or cancellation of the statutory licence of the REIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the body corporate's AML/CFT failure if the contravention occurred with their knowledge, consent, or neglect; courts can impose custodial sentences of up to 2 years in serious cases, prohibit the director from acting as a manager of a financial institution, and place the director on the AML/CFT blacklist.
